roles.name: Property Controller
roles.metaTitle: CAM Reconciliation Guide for Property Controllers
roles.metaDescription: Property controllers: stop spending Q1 in spreadsheets. CAM reconciliation that catches gross-up errors, cap violations, and GL miscoding before statements go out.
roles.headline: CAM Reconciliation for Property Controllers
roles.subheadline: The person who actually runs the math. And gets blamed when it's wrong.
painPoints: Manually reconciling 20-40 buildings in Q1 using spreadsheets inherited from predecessors
Yardi or MRI configurations that don't match current lease terms, found only when tenants dispute
Gross-up calculations applied to fixed expenses that shouldn't be grossed up
Cap calculations that reset incorrectly after lease renewals
GL accounts added mid-year that never got mapped to recovery pools
roles.typicalWorkflow: January: pull year-end GL export from Yardi or MRI. Load into Excel. Manually reconcile each tenant's estimated payments against actuals. Apply gross-up per lease. Check caps. Generate statements. Send. Repeat for every building. Duration: 6-10 weeks.
roles.timeOnCam: Property controllers handle most CAM reconciliation. At firms with 20 to 50 buildings, it fills much of Q1.
commonErrors: Gross-up applied to fixed expenses (property taxes, insurance) - should only apply to variable costs
Wrong occupancy threshold used for gross-up (lease says 95%, ERP configured at 90%)
Non-cumulative cap applied when lease specifies cumulative: compounds into significant overcharge over time
Pro-rata denominator not updated after tenant move-outs or new construction
GL coding errors not caught until tenant auditor finds them 2 years later
roles.capveriValue: Upload your ERP export. CapVeri recalculates every tenant's reconciliation from scratch, independently of your ERP's configuration, and flags every discrepancy with the specific lease clause it violates. Catches the errors before statements go out instead of after tenant auditors find them.
roles.timeSavings: CapVeri works out each building again from the source data. Your controllers review and approve the results. They no longer rebuild every reconciliation by hand.

roles.name: CFO / Financial Controller
roles.metaTitle: CAM Reconciliation ROI for CFOs and Financial Controllers
roles.metaDescription: CFOs: model CAM billing-error exposure per building with the ROI calculator. See the recovery model and liability exposure before your next reconciliation cycle.
roles.headline: CAM Reconciliation for CFOs and Financial Controllers
roles.subheadline: The NOI leakage you can't see, until a tenant auditor finds it for you.
painPoints: No visibility into whether CAM reconciliation math is correct until a tenant dispute surfaces
Audit exposure: tenant-side auditors (Tango Analytics, Visual Lease) are hired on contingency to find errors landlords missed
Revenue leakage from systematic underbilling (gross-up errors, missed expense categories, cap calculation mistakes)
SB 1103 response risk in California: failure to respond to qualified commercial tenant requests within 30 days triggers treble-damage liability
Year-end close delays because reconciliation process takes too long
roles.typicalWorkflow: CFOs review CAM reconciliation at a high level: total billings vs. budget, aggregate recovery ratios, and any disputes flagged by property managers. Reconciliation details are delegated to property controllers. CFO involvement spikes when a tenant disputes or files an audit request.
roles.timeOnCam: CFOs spend part of Q1 on CAM review and disputes. It grows in years when tenants hire outside auditors.
commonErrors: No independent verification of ERP output: trusting Yardi or MRI to self-report errors
Systematic underbilling not discovered until acquisition due diligence exposes it
Liability from SB 1103 non-compliance in California not on the radar
Recovery ratio variance between properties never explained or investigated
Capital expenses flowing through operating expense pools (billing tenants for CapEx)
roles.capveriValue: CapVeri gives CFOs a portfolio-level view of CAM recovery gaps, liability exposure, and reconciliation accuracy, without requiring technical knowledge of ERP configuration. {{pricing.trialCopy}} Run it before your Q1 reconciliation cycle to establish baseline leakage.
roles.timeSavings: ROI model: modeled recovery range of $5,900-$35,300 per building depending on CAM pool size and lease complexity. With {{pricing.launchOfferTerms}}, a mid-scenario recovery of ~$17,700 represents strong ROI per building.

roles.name: Lease Administrator
roles.metaTitle: CAM Reconciliation Guide for Lease Administrators
roles.metaDescription: Lease administrators: track CAM exclusions, audit rights, and cap clauses across your entire portfolio. Catch misapplied lease terms before tenants do.
roles.headline: CAM Reconciliation for Lease Administrators
roles.subheadline: The clause-level detail that makes or breaks every reconciliation
painPoints: Tracking CAM exclusions across 50-200 leases, each with slightly different language
Lease amendments that change exclusion lists, cap types, or gross-up thresholds, not reflected in ERP settings
Audit rights clause management: knowing when and how tenants can request records
Base year resets after lease renewals: calculated and applied correctly across multiple tenants
Capital expenditure misclassification: CapEx flowing through operating expense pools
roles.typicalWorkflow: Lease admins maintain the lease abstract database. During reconciliation season, they verify that ERP configuration matches current lease terms for each tenant. They flag discrepancies to property controllers. They also field tenant audit requests and manage the response process.
roles.timeOnCam: Lease administrators spend much of Q1 checking ERP settings against lease terms. This manual work relies on spreadsheets and PDFs.
commonErrors: Exclusion lists not updated after lease amendments: capital expenses slipping into CAM pools
Base year amounts not updated after the renewal base year: tenants charged on wrong baseline
Audit rights clause not tracked: missing tenant request deadlines creates liability
Different gross-up thresholds per lease not reflected in ERP: single pool-level threshold applied to all tenants
Management fee caps buried in lease riders that never made it into the ERP
roles.capveriValue: CapVeri's lease abstraction layer lets lease admins map each tenant's specific CAM clauses and validates that reconciliation output matches those terms. Every discrepancy is flagged with the specific clause and the dollar impact.
roles.timeSavings: CapVeri matches ERP settings to each lease term for you. Your team skips comparing ERP output to lease PDFs tenant by tenant. The lease terms drive every flag.

roles.name: Property Accountant
roles.metaTitle: CAM Reconciliation Guide for Property Accountants
roles.metaDescription: Property accountants: automate GL coding validation, expense categorization, and CAM pool reconciliation. Stop manually tracing miscoded entries at year-end.
roles.headline: CAM Reconciliation for Property Accountants
roles.subheadline: GL coding errors compound every year. Catch them before year-end close.
painPoints: GL coding errors from property management staff that flow into CAM pools incorrectly
Expense categorization that doesn't match lease definitions for recoverable vs. non-recoverable
Journal entries at year-end to correct miscoded transactions, then reconciling those corrections through CAM billing
New vendor categories created mid-year that don't map to recovery pools
Capital vs. operating expense classification disputes that affect CAM pool totals
roles.typicalWorkflow: Property accountants maintain the GL, post journal entries, and close each period. During reconciliation season, they work with property controllers to ensure GL balances flow correctly to recovery pool exports. They investigate variances between GL totals and recovery pool calculations.
roles.timeOnCam: Property accountants spend part of Q1 on CAM-related GL work. That means coding reviews, recoding, and export prep.
commonErrors: Vendor invoices coded to wrong GL accounts: repairs and maintenance vs. capital improvements
Management fees posted to wrong account: not linked to recovery pool, or grossed up incorrectly
Utilities split incorrectly between common area and tenant-specific: common area portion missing from pool
Insurance premium true-ups not prorated correctly through CAM billing
Reserves classified as operating expenses: capital reserves are generally not recoverable
roles.capveriValue: CapVeri's GL analysis layer flags suspicious coding patterns: unusual accounts, amounts that don't match historical patterns, and capital expenditures that may have slipped into operating expense pools. Advisory flags only. Your team makes the final call.
roles.timeSavings: CapVeri flags unusual GL items for you at year-end. Your team reviews what it flags. No more hunting line by line.

roles.name: Asset Manager
roles.metaTitle: CAM Reconciliation for Asset Managers: NOI Impact & Portfolio
roles.metaDescription: Asset managers: CAM billing errors reduce NOI and create audit exposure at acquisition. See portfolio-level leakage and recovery ratio variance across all buildings.
roles.headline: CAM Reconciliation for Asset Managers
roles.subheadline: CAM leakage is a NOI problem. It's invisible until you measure it.
painPoints: No portfolio-level view of CAM recovery ratios: only property-level data from each controller
Acquisition due diligence: inherited CAM billing errors that reduce NOI projections
Recovery ratio variance between comparable buildings not explained or investigated
Tenant disputes that surface during asset disposition. They are solvable earlier at lower cost.
Cap structure analysis across portfolio: which buildings have cumulative vs. non-cumulative caps and what that means for 5-year NOI
roles.typicalWorkflow: Asset managers review portfolio operating performance quarterly. CAM recovery is a line item in property-level financials. Disputes surface as line items in property management reports. Asset managers engage deeply with CAM only during acquisitions (due diligence) or dispositions (disclosure obligations).
roles.timeOnCam: Asset managers spend some of Q1 reviewing CAM. It spikes when they buy buildings or when tenants hire auditors.
commonErrors: Accepting acquisition underwriting CAM recovery figures without independent verification
Not modeling cumulative cap carry-forward in NOI projections: underestimates future recovery
Recovery ratio benchmarking against wrong peer set: office vs. retail norms are very different
SB 1103 liability not included in California asset risk assessments
Tenant audit exposure not quantified before disposition: emerges as post-closing claim
roles.capveriValue: CapVeri's portfolio view gives asset managers building-level recovery gap analysis, CAP structure modeling, and leakage estimates across their entire portfolio. Run a full portfolio audit before acquisition or disposition to quantify CAM risk.
roles.timeSavings: Use the ROI calculator to model undetected CAM leakage per building during acquisition due diligence. At portfolio scale, recovered leakage can mean meaningful NOI uplift from existing assets, without adding new square footage.

roles.name: Director of Property Management
roles.metaTitle: CAM Reconciliation for Property Management Directors
roles.metaDescription: Property management directors: standardize CAM reconciliation across your team. Reduce Q1 crunch time, catch errors before disputes, and scale to 50 buildings.
roles.headline: CAM Reconciliation for Directors of Property Management
roles.subheadline: Scale your team's capacity without scaling headcount
painPoints: Q1 crunch requires all-hands: property managers, controllers, and accountants overwhelmed simultaneously
No standardized reconciliation process: each controller has their own method, spreadsheet, and error rate
Disputes from prior years still being managed while new cycle starts
New team members take 2-3 years to fully understand CAM reconciliation nuances
Adding buildings to the portfolio increases workload linearly, with no economies of scale
roles.typicalWorkflow: Directors oversee the reconciliation process from a management perspective: setting timelines, allocating staff, resolving escalated issues, and reviewing statements before they go out. They also field calls from tenants and tenant representatives during dispute season.
roles.timeOnCam: Directors of property management spend much of Q1 on reconciliation. They review output, manage disputes, and coordinate teams.
commonErrors: Inconsistent reconciliation methodology across buildings: no standardized process for gross-up, caps, or exclusions
Statements sent without independent review: errors discovered by tenants instead of internally
Dispute backlog from prior years consuming current-year capacity
Onboarding new properties without standardized CAM setup verification
No benchmarking of reconciliation timing against industry peers: 90-day statements are avoidable
roles.capveriValue: CapVeri standardizes the reconciliation process across your entire portfolio. Every building follows the same methodology. Every statement gets independently verified against lease terms before it goes out. Directors get a single dashboard view of reconciliation status, errors found, and statements ready for review.
roles.timeSavings: CapVeri runs the same method on every building. Your controllers review and approve instead of building each reconciliation from scratch.
